Annex E: Further information on social value and value for money

PPN 026 does not replace the requirements included in other guidance documents or legislation. You should ensure that you follow the expectations set out elsewhere and where your legal obligations conflict with the PPN 026, you must meet your legal obligations.

You are also able to take into account broader social value expectations, such as carbon emissions or modern slavery as set out in other PPNs or with their own weighting in your procurements. However, this should be in addition to the 10% or 20% weighting applied to the Social Value Model and not form part of this weighting. There may also be opportunities to use the existing outcomes in ways that align with your wider organisation objectives, for example, by encouraging the creation of jobs or skills as a part of a talent pipeline in the clean energy industry if your organisation has environmental objectives and this is appropriate for your contract.

1. The Green Book

The government uses the Green Book to evaluate policies, projects, and programmes to ensure public money is spent effectively. By applying Green Book principles, decision-makers can select proposals that achieve their intended objectives while delivering improved social welfare and community benefits. For further details on how to handle public funds, refer to the Managing public money guidance.

2. Public Services (Social Value) Act 2012

When procuring services, or services together with goods and/or works, you should have regard to the Public Services (Social Value) Act 2012[footnote 21] to ensure your procurement is compliant. It requires public authorities in England and Wales (with some exceptions in Wales) to consider when procuring services;

how what is being proposed might improve the economic, social, and environmental wellbeing of the relevant area

how in conducting the process of procurement, it might act with a view to securing that improvement

whether to take and consultation on the above points

The Social Value Model is designed to align with the Public Services (Social Value) Act 2012, however, as part of your business case process and before the procurement begins, you should ensure that you have given due regard to the Act.

3. The National Procurement Policy Statement

The Procurement Act 2023 sets out that contracting authorities must have regard to the National Procurement Policy Statement (NPPS) when procuring public contracts, unless they are exempted. The NPPS sets the government’s strategic priorities for public procurement in support of the government’s missions whilst still achieving value for money and social value.

You should avoid changing the criteria and sub-criteria if possible because they are designed to be ready to use without change. This reduces the burden of running procurements and provides consistency for suppliers.

3.3. Set an evaluation methodology

You must be transparent with potential suppliers about the evaluation criteria and evaluation process, as with all public contracts.

The evaluating panel should use the Social Value Model question award criteria and your selected award criteria and sub-criteria to evaluate and score bids. You should establish an evaluation methodology (the way bids are scored) appropriate for your contract and ensure the evaluating panel scores the responses using the methodology published in your tender documents.

You should design an effective, objective and non-discriminatory scoring methodology that suits the contract and enables clear differentiation between tenders. Use scoring bands or a method that clearly differentiates suppliers’ responses to the Social Value Model question. Annex C sets out an example method. However, you should always use a scoring approach that best fits your wider procurement and commercial objectives.

Refer to the Sourcing Playbook and Bid Evaluation Guidance Note[footnote 7] for more information on evaluation methodologies. You should seek legal advice when deciding upon assessment methodologies if needed.

3.4. Test outcomes

When conducting market engagement, you must remain compliant with the Procurement Act[footnote 8], which includes a requirement to publish a preliminary market engagement notice if preliminary market engagement is carried out. Preliminary market engagement can help you develop a high-quality procurement with more successful social value outcomes.

During preliminary market engagement you should test the selected Social Value Model outcomes, criteria, sub-criteria, and metrics with potential suppliers to confirm your selection is still relevant to the subject matter of the contract, proportionate, and non-discriminatory. You can hold engagement events with potential suppliers to better understand what affects the cost, quality, and efficiency of delivering social value.

You can increase the Social Value Model weighting above the minimum requirement to create more or better jobs, skills, and opportunities for local communities in well-established and capable markets. This should be balanced with ensuring your contract remains deliverable, provides value for money and compliance with legal duties.

4. Procure

In the ‘Procure’ stage you will create and publish the tender documentation needed to run a procurement, evaluate tenders, and award and commence your contract.

Competitive Tendering Procedures

You should assess social value as an award criteria, not as a condition of participation. The Social Value Model is designed to be incorporated in either an open or competitive flexible procedure (as well as the establishment of a framework and subsequent call offs).

You should consider if a short dialogue stage, or the option to do so, would provide an opportunity to ensure social value commitments are clear, deliverable, and optimised, if using a competitive flexible procedure. You can apply the social value evaluation, as with other award criteria, to limit the number of participating suppliers invited to participate in further stages of a competitive flexible procedure. As always, the criteria by which you choose suppliers to proceed must be in the tender notice or associated procurement documents.

If it is necessary to amend or refine your social value evaluation criteria, this must be done in accordance with the Procurement Act[footnote 9].

4.1. Set the Social Value Model question

You should include the Social Value Model question below and include the Social Value Model outcome and corresponding criteria and sub-criteria.

Social Value Model Question

In no more than [number of words] please set out the specific, measurable and time bound commitment(s) your organisation will make to deliver [Social Value Model outcome] in [the relevant area].

Your response will be assessed against the sub criteria and following additional award criteria:

1. The response supports one or more Community Programmes evidenced by a dated letter to the Community Programme/s listed contact, confirming that, subject to the award of the contract, you will support the programme and that this is additional to any support proposed or currently offered and/or provided.

Or, if the response is not supporting one or more Community Programmes:

2. The response includes all of the following:

a. a description of how the commitment meets the award criteria and sub-criteria

b. a specific target cohort, or details of how you will identify and define a target cohort (if not already identified by the contracting authority)

c. a description of how you will identify and reach the target cohort, how you will design or refine and tailor the offer to the target cohort

d. a description of how you will engage with staff, suppliers, customers and communities (as appropriate) through the delivery of the contract to deliver the social value commitment. For example, engagement, co-design or creation, training and education, partnering or collaborating, and volunteering
